notes: SUPERSEDES the prior UNVERIFIED verdict (probed_at 2026-09-21T10:55:47Z), which was scored on a project with zero exploratory sessions (every figure zeroed, sessions:[] and top_testers:[]). That is no longer the case: write probes since created session 779 (ES-14, active, 2 logs - one bug, one note carrying linked defect TM-1234) and session 780 (ES-15, a clone of 779 with 2 copied logs). Re-verified live here (setup step 2) before probing: both sessions are active, created_by is a real user (id 2522, 'ing'), and each carries summary {bug:1, note:1}. RE-PROBE RESULT, STILL UNVERIFIED - two independent reasons: (1) UNFALSIFIABLE CONTRACT, RE-CONFIRMED: describeCapability was re-checked this run and the 200 schema still declares `data` as a bare `{type: object}` with a prose description only - zero enumerated properties. Per this campaign's settled rule (three other tm capabilities already carry this same flag in check-contract.py) an unfalsifiable contract can never register DRIFT and must not be counted as a clean PASS either, regardless of how sensible or well-populated the actual response looks. This alone caps the verdict below PASS/DRIFT no matter what the data shows. (2) EMPTY-CASE STILL OPEN FOR top_testers: even with 2 sessions, 4 logs and 2 confirmed bugs, top_testers came back [] in all three attempts (both modes, and the single-session and two-session scopes). The declared item shape `{user, bug_count}` remains completely unexercised - this is the named empty case from the task and it is being named here explicitly, not folded into a pass. Working hypothesis for WHY it stays empty: list_exploratory_sessions' own guidance says assignee/created_by/closed_by are resolved separately, and both probe sessions have assignee:null (confirmed in setup step 2) despite having a real created_by. If top_testers is ranked off assignee rather than created_by/log-author, an unassigned session can never contribute a top tester no matter how many bugs it logs - which would mean this capability's populated-vs-empty behavior for top_testers depends on a write path (assign_test_run_owner or session assignment) that the write probes never exercised. This is a plausible but UNCONFIRMED explanation, offered as a lead for whoever runs the next write-probe wave, not stated as fact. RELATED PARTIAL GAP - assignee expansion: the contract says sessions[].assignee is 'expanded from ids into user objects server-side, and come back null for a tester who is no longer a TM user.' Both sessions here return assignee:null, but list_exploratory_sessions confirms this is because no assignee was ever set (not because a former assignee's account is gone) - so the 'expanded to a real user object' branch of this field is still never actually exercised either; only the null branch is, and for a different reason than the one the contract names. MODE COMPARISON (session_selection vs time_period): both modes were exercised against the same two sessions (attempt 1 vs attempt 2) and returned byte-identical `data` shapes and values - no divergence was found. This capability does NOT reproduce the sibling defect seen on list_workspace_fields (conditional `info` by mode); the mode-selection risk flagged in the task did not materialize here. COUNT-VS-ROWS CHECK, PASSES: outcomes.bugs_found=2 for the two-session query matches the sum of sessions[].summary.bug (1+1=2) - the clone's (780's) logs ARE counted in the aggregate, not silently dropped. Cross-checked further with a single-session query (attempt 3, session_ids=779 alone): outcomes.bugs_found=1, matching sessions[0].summary.bug=1 and matching a sibling probe's independently-reported number for session 779 in isolation. So the aggregate-vs-row arithmetic is internally consistent here - this capability does NOT show the count-vs-rows defect this wave was watching for, despite the pattern hitting five other capabilities in this campaign.
